items.title: Organizing Elements using pack(), grid(), and place()

source_refs.note: Unnumbered topic Organizing Elements using pack(), grid(), and place() as printed (PDF 52-54, printed 48-50); its own lesson since 2026-10-29 (one lesson per book heading), moved from the topic 4.1 lesson.

blocks.text: The pack() method places widgets in a simple vertical or horizontal order. It is easy to use and works well for small applications. The grid() method arranges widgets in rows and columns like a table. It is useful for forms and structured layouts. The place() method positions widgets at exact locations on the window (as shown in Figure 4.2). It gives more control but needs careful adjustment.

blocks.alt: Three windows side by side. Pack(): Button 1, Button 2 and Button 3 stacked one below another in the centre. Grid(): Button 1 and Button 2 side by side in a row, with a wide Button 3 spanning both columns below. Place(): Button 1 at the top left, Button 2 lower down on the right, and Button 3 at the bottom left.
blocks.caption: Figure 4.2: Diagram showing Tkinter Layout Managers: pack(), grid(), place() (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 4.2).

blocks.text:
import tkinter as tk

# Create main window
window = tk.Tk()
window.title("pack()")
window.geometry("300x220")

# Create buttons
button1 = tk.Button(window, text="Button 1", width=12)
button2 = tk.Button(window, text="Button 2", width=12)
button3 = tk.Button(window, text="Button 3", width=12)

# Arrange buttons using pack()
button1.pack(pady=10)
button2.pack(pady=10)
button3.pack(pady=10)

# Run the application
window.mainloop()

import tkinter as tk

# Create main window
window = tk.Tk()
window.title("grid()")
window.geometry("300x220")

# Create buttons
button1 = tk.Button(window, text="Button 1", width=10)
button2 = tk.Button(window, text="Button 2", width=10)
button3 = tk.Button(window, text="Button 3", width=24)

# Arrange buttons using grid()
button1.grid(row=0, column=0, padx=10, pady=20)
button2.grid(row=0, column=1, padx=10, pady=20)

# Button 3 spans two columns
button3.grid(row=1, column=0, columnspan=2, padx=10, pady=10)

# Keep content centred
window.grid_columnconfigure(0, weight=1)
window.grid_columnconfigure(1, weight=1)

# Run the application
window.mainloop()

import tkinter as tk

# Create main window
window = tk.Tk()
window.title("place()")
window.geometry("300x220")

# Create buttons
button1 = tk.Button(window, text="Button 1", width=10)
button2 = tk.Button(window, text="Button 2", width=10)
button3 = tk.Button(window, text="Button 3", width=10)

# Arrange buttons using place()
button1.place(x=30, y=40)
button2.place(x=170, y=85)
button3.place(x=30, y=140)

# Run the application
window.mainloop()
